reading.body:
Governance is the dominant differentiating claim across this set of enterprise AI platforms, appearing in nearly every product note as audit logs, RBAC, guardrails, permission-aware retrieval, or data access controls.

That pattern reflects where enterprise procurement pressure currently sits. Buyers deploying agents across service desks, customer support, and internal knowledge systems need to answer questions about who can see what, what the agent did, and how errors are caught. The tools here respond to that demand more visibly than they compete on raw model capability, which most treat as interchangeable, Decagon's model-agnostic positioning being the clearest statement of that posture.

The data covers eight vendors, six US-headquartered and two European, with Cognigy being the only one to name GDPR compliance and EU-hosted deployment as explicit product features. That single data point gestures at jurisdictional fragmentation in enterprise AI procurement but does not quantify it. Nothing in this dataset speaks to compute consumption, power draw, or infrastructure footprint, so no connection to those constraints can be drawn from it. What it does capture is a software layer sitting above the models and the data centers, where orchestration and control, not raw scale, are the current product surface.
